Exact command: `node --import ./scripts/mutation-network-deny.mjs --import ./test/setup-env.mjs --test --test-reporter=tap --test-force-exit test/conversation-pool.test.js` -> `# tests 27 / # pass 27 / # fail 0 / # skipped 0 / # todo 0`, IDENTICAL over six consecutive runs. Re-measured with the harness's OWN counting semantics: scripts/mutation-harness-utils.mjs is both the harness helper and its structured reporter and throws at import on Windows ('mutation harness requires git at a trusted absolute path'), so tmp/harness-reporter.mjs is a verbatim copy of its reporter half used as `--test-reporter=./tmp/harness-reporter.mjs`; the aggregate summary was {tests 27, failed 0, passed 27, cancelled 0, skipped 0, todo 0, topLevel 6, suites 6}, IDENTICAL over four consecutive runs and equal to the TAP counts. This spec names ONE test file, so the harness's combined invocation and a per-file invocation are the same argv by construction and there is no per-file-vs-combined gap to report. DRIFT DISCLOSURE: per-file counts in this repo are known to drift between identical CI runs (2026-09-13 measurement: test/cascade-native-bridge.test.js reported 61 in one CI run and 68 in another; twelve identical runs of another file produced eleven distinct counts). No drift was reproducible for THIS file locally (10/10 runs identical at 27), and this suite is synchronous pure-function assertion over src/conversation-pool.js with no timers of its own, no post-import env reads and no child processes, which is why it was chosen ahead of the other unpinned modules. If guard 2 still rejects 27 on the Linux runner, that is the correct loud outcome: re-measure there with `node scripts/spec-baseline-audit.mjs conversation-pool-fingerprint-guards` and change the number, do NOT narrow the mutations to make it start.
_scope_note: src/conversation-pool.js had zero mutation specs before this file (audit 2026-09-13: 35 of 77 non-vendor src files pinned, and this 33 KB module was one of the four largest unpinned ones). Every mutation below targets the reuse FINGERPRINT contract, because a silent change there does not throw: the pool just misses every turn (or worse, hits a cascade that belongs to different content), and every remaining test in the tree stays green.

mutations.name: priorTurnsForBefore no longer refuses a single-turn conversation — with no prior turn to digest, every first turn for the same caller/model produces the SAME fingerprint (the empty trajectory), so a brand-new conversation can check out an unrelated cascade instead of starting fresh

priorTurnsForBefore stops dropping the newest user/tool turn (slice end +1) — the 'before' fingerprint now describes a state that has not happened yet, so after(turn1) no longer equals before(turn2) and the cascade we just stored can never be looked up again: reuse degrades to a fresh cascade every turn, silently

stripMetaTags stops applying stripMetaTagSpans — the client-injected tags that change every turn (cwd snapshot, todo state, hook output) go back into the hash, which is exactly issue #24: the fingerprint drifts on every request and Cascade reuse silently falls back to fresh for the whole session

the assistant text projection stops collapsing internal whitespace — a client that re-renders the same prior answer with different spacing (markdown reflow, stream reassembly) hashes differently, so the next turn misses the cascade we just stored and the model re-reads the whole history

systemDigest returns '' unconditionally — the pre-audit default, where two different system prompts share one fingerprint, so a caller is handed a cascade resumed under someone else's system context instead of missing
an image block with no stable id becomes hashable again — distinct unhashable media collide into one fingerprint instead of disabling reuse for that request, so the wrong image can be resumed against

checkin drops the inherited ttlHintMs when the caller passes no hint (audit MED-2) — an entry that was written under an Anthropic 1h prompt-cache marker loses the hint on the next round-trip, so the 1h cache window silently collapses back to the 30-minute pool default

KNOWN SURVIVOR — checkout drops the entry-vs-request callerKey comparison, so a pooled entry may be handed to a request whose callerKey differs. Not covered by design, and not reachable through the public API today: callerKey is itself hashed into the key payload (buildKeyPayload sets `caller`), so two different callers never produce the same fingerprint and the branch cannot fire. The suite's caller-isolation assertions compare two DIFFERENT fingerprints and therefore pass with or without this line. It is defence in depth for a future key layout that drops caller from the payload — if that refactor ever happens, this mutation starts being caught and this spec will say so.

_not_covered: Three invariants in this module are NOT pinned, because no existing assertion drives them. All three were MEASURED with a throwaway probe spec (tmp/uncovered-probe.json, gitignored, same reporter and argv as this spec): each of the three mutations below was applied and the suite stayed green, so these are recorded findings rather than guesses. (1) Deleting `.sort()` from `Object.keys(v).sort()` in stableStringify survives — the test named 'object key order in mixed content is stable' passes anyway, because canonicalContentBlock builds its image record itself ({type, url}) with a fixed key order, so caller key order never reaches stableStringify through that path; the routes where it does are the unknown-typed-block fallback (`json: stableStringify(part)`) and the parsed tool-call arguments digest, and neither has a test that feeds two orderings of the same object. (2) invalidateFor's second-pass sibling cleanup (audit H-2) is unpinned: it only matters when one cascadeId is indexed under several fingerprint slots (checkin with an array) or an alias slot carries a different apiKey, and test/conversation-pool.test.js never builds an alias slot, so `if (!drop && e.cascadeId && targetCascadeIds.has(e.cascadeId)) drop = true;` can be disabled with the suite staying green. (3) The REUSE_BY_CALLER caller-fallback index is off by default (CASCADE_REUSE_BY_CALLER must be '1' at module load) and no test sets it, so _callerFallbackCheckout is dead code under the test environment; making it inert (`const fp = null;`) survives.
